mainTopic: Greek language versus חכמת יוונית; the rules about keeping dogs; how far pigeon traps must be from a settled area
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about Greek. רבי and רבי יוסי praise speaking Greek or Persian, so the גמרא answers that the Greek language is allowed and only חכמת יוונית is forbidden. It then asks why רבן גמליאל's household studied חכמת יוונית, and answers that they were close to the government and so received a special permission, as a ברייתא confirms. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה that a person may keep a dog only if it is chained. A ברייתא allows a border town to let its dog loose at night, and רב נחמן says בבל counts as a border town, which the גמרא limits to נהרדעא. רבי אליעזר הגדול compares raising dogs to raising pigs. A דרשה and a sad story show how a dog's bark can frighten a pregnant woman into losing her baby. Finally the גמרא discusses how far from a settled area one must be to set pigeon traps, and the פרק מרובה comes to a close.

steps.title: רבי and רבי יוסי prefer Hebrew, Greek or Persian over the local Aramaic
steps.stepSummary: The challenge continues. רבי says that in ארץ ישראל one should speak Hebrew or Greek, not Syriac. רבי יוסי says the same about בבל: speak Hebrew or Persian, not Aramaic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why speak Syriac? Speak either the holy tongue or Greek! And רבי יוסי said: In בבל, why speak Aramaic? Speak either the holy tongue or Persian!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי, who praises Greek, and adds a similar line from רבי יוסי. This is used to challenge the ruling that Greek wisdom is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said a person is cursed if he teaches his son חכמת יוונית. But רבי openly recommends speaking Greek. So how can anything Greek be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: Syriac, a local Aramaic dialect spoken in ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: This step begins in the middle of a sentence. The words before it, said by רבי, are: 'In ארץ ישראל,' so the full line is 'In ארץ ישראל, why speak Syriac?'

phrases.english: Why the Syriac language?
phrases.notes: This continues רבי's words from just before: in ארץ ישראל, why speak Syriac?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, אוֹ לָשׁוֹן יְוָנִית!
phrases.english: Either the holy tongue, or the Greek language!
And Rabbi Yosei said:
In Babylonia – why the Aramaic language?
phrases.notes: The square brackets add the letter ב, so it reads 'in בבל.'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, אוֹ לָשׁוֹן פָּרְסִי!
phrases.english: Either the holy tongue, or the Persian language!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָשׁוֹן סוּרְסִי לָמָּה? אוֹ לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, אוֹ לָשׁוֹן יְוָנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that began before this section, against the ban on חכמת יוונית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that teaching חכמת יוונית is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי recommends speaking Greek, then Greek should not be forbidden.

steps.title: The Greek language and Greek wisdom are two different things
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the Greek language is allowed. Only Greek wisdom is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: the Greek language is one thing, and Greek wisdom is another thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating two things: speaking Greek, and studying Greek wisdom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי praised speaking the Greek language. The ban was only on חכמת יוונית. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate, a thing of its own
Greek wisdom, a kind of Greek learning that was forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix these up: speaking Greek is fine. Only חכמת יוונית is the problem.

phrases.english: They say: the Greek language is separate,
and Greek wisdom is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָשׁוֹן יְוָנִי לְחוּד, חׇכְמַת יְוָנִית לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי and רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything Greek might be forbidden, so praising Greek would contradict the ban.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only חכמת יוונית is forbidden. The Greek language is allowed.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's household studied Greek wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether Greek wisdom is really forbidden. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that 500 children in his father's house studied it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is Greek wisdom really forbidden? But רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: 'My eye has hurt my soul, because of all the daughters of my city.' There were a thousand children in my father's house. Five hundred studied תורה and five hundred studied Greek wisdom. None of them survived except me, here, and my father's brother's son, in Asia.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא attacks the answer itself: is חכמת יוונית really forbidden? It brings a story showing that the house of a great נשיא taught it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is mourning the children of his father's house, and he mentions that half of them learned חכמת יוונית. If it were forbidden, why would רבן גמליאל's house teach it so openly?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it forbidden? A question that expects 'no'
But didn't he say...? Introduces a challenge from a source

phrases.english: And is Greek wisdom forbidden?!
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Shmuel said
in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
"My eye has hurt my soul
because of all the daughters of my city" –
there were a thousand children in my father's house;
five hundred of them studied Torah,
five hundred studied Greek wisdom;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר מֵהֶם אֶלָּא אֲנִי – כָּאן,
phrases.english: and none of them remained except me – here,
and my father's brother's son – in Asia!
phrases.notes: עסיא is a place name, the region called Asia Minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחׇכְמַת יְוָנִית מִי אֲסִירָא?! וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 2 that חכמת יוונית is forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חכמת יוונית is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The house of רבן גמליאל, the leader of the generation, openly taught it to 500 children.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's household was an exception because of its ties to the government
steps.stepSummary: The house of רבן גמליאל is different, because they dealt closely with the ruling government.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: The house of רבן גמליאל is different, because they were close to the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ban stays in place, but this family had a special permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against חכמת יוונית does not change. רבן גמליאל's family needed to deal with the government, so they were given an exception. This is a special case, not proof that the subject is allowed for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different; a case that stands apart from the rule
Close to the government, people who deal with the rulers

phrases.english: They say: The house of Rabban Gamliel is different,
as they were close to the government.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבן גמליאל's household.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special exception for a particular group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבן גמליאל's house taught חכמת יוונית, maybe it is allowed for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden in general. Only those close to the government were allowed.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows exceptions for people close to the government
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the answer. The Roman 'komi' haircut is a forbidden gentile custom, but אבטולמוס בר ראובן was allowed it, and רבן גמליאל's house was allowed חכמת יוונית, all because they were close to the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One who cuts his hair in the komi style, this is one of the ways of the Amorites. They allowed אבטולמוס בר ראובן to cut his hair komi style, because he was close to the government. They allowed the house of רבן גמליאל to discuss Greek wisdom, because they were close to the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says outright what it just answered: the house of רבן גמליאל was allowed חכמת יוונית because of its government ties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that חז"ל did make exceptions for people who had to deal with the rulers. It gives two examples: a haircut and חכמת יוונית. The second example matches our answer exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: And as was taught in a ברייתא; brings support
One who gets the komi haircut, a Roman style
Ways of the Amorites, forbidden gentile customs

steps.whatToRemember: Greek language is allowed. חכמת יוונית is forbidden, except for people like רבן גמליאל's household who needed it because they dealt with the government.

phrases.english: And as it is taught:
One who cuts his hair in the komi style –
this is from the ways of the Amorites.
Avtolmos bar Reuven –
they permitted him to cut his hair komi style,
because he was close to the government.
Those of the house of Rabban Gamliel –
they permitted them to discuss Greek wisdom,
because they were close to the government.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 4 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל's household had a special permission for חכמת יוונית because of government ties
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the komi haircut and about רבן גמליאל's household
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חכמת יוונית remains forbidden. Those close to the government were given an exception.

steps.title: The משנה: a dog may only be raised if chained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a person may not raise a dog unless it is tied with chains.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not raise a dog unless it is tied with chains, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה to set up a discussion about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new section. The rule is that a person may keep a dog only if it is chained. The steps that follow explain why dogs are treated so strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not raise or keep
Etc.; the rest of the משנה line

phrases.english: A person may not raise a dog

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן קָשׁוּר בְּשַׁלְשְׁלָאוֹת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: unless it is tied with chains, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יְגַדֵּל אָדָם אֶת הַכֶּלֶב אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן קָשׁוּר בְּשַׁלְשְׁלָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dog may only be kept if it is chained.

steps.title: A ברייתא: border towns may keep a dog loose at night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats the rule and adds that in a city near the border, one may keep a dog, tie it by day, and let it loose at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person may not raise a dog unless it is tied with a chain. But he may raise one in a city that is near the border, and tie it during the day and let it loose at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds an exception to the משנה's rule about dogs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule still holds: keep a dog chained. A city near the border is a special case, and there the dog may be let loose at night. During the day it must still be tied.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; introduces a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Dogs must be chained. In a border town, one may let the dog loose at night, but it must be tied during the day.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person may not raise a dog –
unless it is tied with a chain.
But he may raise one
in a city that is close to the border,
and he ties it by day and releases it at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יְגַדֵּל אָדָם אֶת הַכֶּלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's rule about dogs with a ברייתא that adds an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a border town one may keep a dog, tied by day and loose at night.

steps.title: Raising dogs is like raising pigs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר הגדול: one who raises dogs is like one who raises pigs.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר הגדול says that someone who raises dogs is like someone who raises pigs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that adds a strong statement about people who raise dogs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that keeping a dog untied is forbidden. רבי אליעזר הגדול goes further and compares a dog-raiser to a pig-raiser, which is a very harsh comparison. The גמרא will now ask what this comparison adds.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
One who raises dogs is like one who raises pigs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger statement to the dog laws from steps 6 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who raises dogs is compared to one who raises pigs.

steps.title: What difference does the comparison make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the comparison to pig-raising makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the next step. Both things are already forbidden, so what does the comparison add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raising pigs is forbidden, and raising loose dogs is also forbidden. So simply saying 'it is like pigs' seems to teach nothing new. The גמרא wants to know the real point.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what is there a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the comparison in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law the dog-pig comparison teaches, since both are already forbidden.

steps.title: The dog-raiser gets the same curse
steps.stepSummary: The difference is that the dog-raiser falls under the same curse as the pig-raiser.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is that the curse applies to him too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the comparison means the dog-raiser is cursed just like the pig-raiser.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is not about whether it is forbidden. It is about the curse. Whatever curse applies to one who raises pigs also applies to one who raises dogs.

keyTerms.meaning: To have it apply to him

phrases.english: To make him subject to a curse.
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא said 'cursed is one who raises pigs.' Now that same curse is said about dog-raisers too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison means the dog-raiser receives the same curse as the pig-raiser.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously חז״ל viewed keeping dangerous dogs.

steps.title: בבל counts as a border city
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that בבל has the status of a city near the border, where keeping a dog is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: בבל is considered like a city near the border.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן applies the border-city exception from step 7 to בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 7 allowed a dog in a city near the border, tied by day and loose at night. רב נחמן says בבל has that status, so dogs may be kept there in that way.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Naḥman said:
Babylonia is like a city close to the border.
phrases.notes: This is the border-city rule from the ברייתא just before. There you may keep a dog, tied by day and loose at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the border-city exception of step 7 and applies it to בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל has the status of a city near the border regarding keeping dogs.

steps.title: This means only נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'בבל' here means only the city of נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They explained it as referring to נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב נחמן's statement. Not all of בבל is meant, only נהרדעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, one might think dogs are allowed everywhere in בבל. The גמרא limits the exception to נהרדעא, a city that really was near the border.

phrases.english: They explained it: Neharde'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The border-city status applies only to נהרדעא, not all of בבל.
steps.whatToRemember: Dogs may be kept only in a border city, tied by day and loose at night. In בבל this means נהרדעא.

steps.title: The שכינה needs at least 22,000 Jews
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי from בירי learns from a פסוק that the שכינה rests on ישראל only when there are at least 22,000.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסתאי from בירי taught: 'And when it rested, he said: Return, ה׳, to the myriads of the thousands of ישראל.' This teaches that the שכינה does not rest on ישראל when they number fewer than two thousand and two myriads.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי gives a דרשה that sets up the next step, which shows how a barking dog can cause great damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the plural words 'myriads' and 'thousands,' which means at least two of each. Two myriads (20,000) plus two thousand equals 22,000. Fewer than that, and the שכינה does not rest on ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dostai from Biri taught:
"And when it rested, he said:
Return, O Lord, to the myriads of the thousands of Israel."

phrases.aramaic: לְלַמֶּדְךָ, שֶׁאֵין שְׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: To teach you that the Divine Presence does not rest on Israel
When they are fewer than two thousand and two myriads.
phrases.notes: The plural words mean at least two of each, so the total is 22,000.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an aggadic teaching that will show the danger of dogs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה rests on ישראל only when they number at least 22,000.

steps.title: A barking dog could drive away the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: If ישראל were one short of 22,000 and a dog's bark made a pregnant woman miscarry, the dog's owner would cause the שכינה to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were missing one, and a pregnant woman among them could have completed the number, and a dog barked at her and she miscarried, then this person caused the שכינה to leave ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי applies his דרשה to dogs. A dog's bark could, in this case, drive the שכינה away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby would have completed the count of 22,000. Because the dog scared the mother into miscarrying, the count stays one short. The owner of the dog is then responsible for the שכינה leaving.

phrases.english: If they were lacking one,
And there was a pregnant woman among them
Who was fit to complete the number,
And a dog barked at her and she miscarried,
It turns out that this one caused
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the owner of the dog.

phrases.english: The Divine Presence to depart from Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָסֵר אַחַת, וְהָיְתָה אִשָּׁה מְעוּבֶּרֶת בֵּינֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 22,000 rule of step 13 to the danger of dogs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dog owner whose dog causes a miscarriage could be responsible for the שכינה leaving ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why raising dogs is treated so harshly: their bark can cause a miscarriage.

steps.title: A story: a dog's bark causes a miscarriage
steps.stepSummary: A woman entering a house to bake was barked at by a dog. The owner said the dog had no fangs, but she answered that it was already too late, because the baby had moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman went into a house to bake, and a dog barked at her. Its owner said to her: Don't be afraid of it, its fangs have been removed. She said to him: Take your kindness and throw it on the thorns, the baby has already moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story that shows the danger it just described. A dog's bark scared a pregnant woman into losing her baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner thought the dog was harmless because it could not bite. But the harm comes from the fright, not only from biting. That is why even a 'safe' dog must be kept tied.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the dog was safe because it had no teeth. The damage here came from the fright of the bark, not from a bite.
steps.whatToRemember: A dog is dangerous even without biting, because its bark can frighten people. This is why the גמרא is so strict about keeping dogs.

phrases.english: A certain woman who entered
To bake in a certain house,
A dog barked at her.
Its owner said to her:
Do not be afraid of it,
Its fangs have been removed.
She said to him:
Take your kindness and throw it on the thorns,
phrases.notes: A way of saying 'your comfort is useless now, it's too late.'

phrases.english: The baby has already moved.
phrases.notes: She was pregnant and felt the baby shift from the fright, so she knew she would lose it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דְּעַלַּת לְמֵיפָא בְּהָהוּא בֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the danger described in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a dog's bark alone can cause a miscarriage, even if the dog cannot bite.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about a woman frightened by a toothless dog.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about pigeon traps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one may not spread traps for pigeons unless far from a settled area.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: One may not spread out traps for pigeons, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says you may only set pigeon traps thirty ריס, which is four מיל, away from a settled area. The worry is that pigeons belonging to people would get caught. The next steps test whether that distance makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: traps or snares for catching birds
"etc.", meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: One may not spread out traps for pigeons, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of dogs and the שכינה and returns to another rule in the משנה, about trapping pigeons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pigeon traps may only be set thirty ריס (four מיל) away from a settled area.

steps.title: Do pigeons really fly so far?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether pigeons really go four מיל, since a משנה keeps a dovecote only fifty אמות from a city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do pigeons really travel that far? But we learned in a משנה: One must keep a dovecote fifty אמות away from the city!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's distance. Another משנה suggests pigeons only go about fifty אמות from home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שובך must be fifty אמות from the city so its pigeons won't eat the city's crops. That suggests fifty אמות is as far as pigeons go. If so, why does our משנה need a distance of four מיל, which is thousands of אמות?

keyTerms.meaning: do they really go that far?
but we learned in a משנה
one must keep at a distance
a cubit, a measure of length

phrases.english: And do they really go that far?
But didn't we learn: One must distance the dovecote
fifty cubits from the city!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distance given in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of thirty ריס (four מיל) distance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה sets fifty אמות for a dovecote, which implies pigeons don't go farther than that. So four מיל seems far too much.

steps.title: אביי: they fly far but fill up nearby
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that pigeons fly much farther, but their bellies are already full within fifty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They fly a lot farther, but their stomachs are full within fifty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by separating flying from eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifty-אמות rule is about eating crops, and pigeons are full after fifty אמות. But they keep flying much farther, so they could still fly into a trap. That's why the trap needs the bigger distance.

phrases.english: Abaye said: They fly around a lot farther,
but their stomachs get full within fifty cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the fifty-אמות משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the two rules measure different things (eating range vs. flying range).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifty-אמות rule shows that pigeons don't go farther than fifty אמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pigeons eat within fifty אמות but fly much farther, so the trap rule needs a larger distance.

steps.title: Only thirty ריס? A ברייתא says even one hundred מיל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if pigeons fly far, why stop at thirty ריס? A ברייתא forbids traps near a settled area even one hundred מיל away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do they fly only thirty ריס and no more? But a ברייתא teaches: In a settled area, one may not spread a trap even one hundred מיל away!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא attacks from the other side: maybe thirty ריס is too short a distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say pigeons fly far, the question is how far. A ברייתא forbids trapping near a settled area even at one hundred מיל. That is much more than the משנה's four מיל, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: a measure of distance; thirty ריס equal four מיל

phrases.english: And they fly thirty ris and no more?
But isn't it taught: In a settled area,
one may not spread a trap even a hundred mil away!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵישָׁט שְׁלֹשִׁים רִיס וְתוּ לָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's answer that pigeons fly far and asks why the limit is only thirty ריס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's limit of thirty ריס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that pigeons can be caught even one hundred מיל from a settlement, so four מיל should not be enough.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a settled area of vineyards
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברייתא is talking about an area full of vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The ברייתא means an area settled with vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that the ברייתא is about a special kind of area, not a regular town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an area of vineyards, pigeons can stop and rest along the way. That lets them fly much farther than usual. So the one hundred מיל case is special, and the משנה's four מיל is the normal rule.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It means a settled area of vineyards.
phrases.notes: The pigeons can rest in the vineyards along the way, so they get much farther.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא of one hundred מיל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ברייתא is about a special kind of area.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means any settled area, which would contradict the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means an area of vineyards where pigeons can rest and fly farther.

steps.title: רבה: a settled area of dovecotes
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a different answer: the ברייתא is talking about an area full of dovecotes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The ברייתא means an area settled with dovecotes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a second answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב יוסף, רבה says the ברייתא is about a place where pigeons can rest. For him, the resting places are dovecotes, not vineyards. This answer sets up the next question.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It means a settled area of dovecotes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same challenge that רב יוסף answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ברייתא is about an area full of dovecotes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means any settled area.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means an area of dovecotes where pigeons can rest, so they reach far distances.

steps.title: Why not forbid it because of the dovecotes themselves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבה: if there are dovecotes nearby, the trap should be forbidden because of those dovecotes, not because of a settlement far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be forbidden simply because of the dovecotes themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trap is set in an area full of dovecotes, those dovecotes' pigeons are right there and could be caught. So the reason for the rule should be the nearby dovecotes. Why does the ברייתא talk about a settlement one hundred מיל away?

keyTerms.meaning: let him derive it (from a simpler reason)

phrases.english: But let him derive it because of
the dovecotes themselves!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's answer from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that the ברייתא is about an area of dovecotes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nearby dovecotes would already forbid the trap, so the far-away settlement should not matter.

steps.title: Three answers: the dovecotes belong to a גוי, to no one, or to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three possible answers: the dovecotes belong to a גוי, are הפקר, or belong to the trapper himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say they belong to a גוי. Or if you want, say they are ownerless. Or if you want, say they are his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by explaining why the nearby dovecotes themselves are not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, catching pigeons from those dovecotes is not taking another Jew's birds: they belong to a גוי, to no one, or to the trapper himself. So the dovecotes don't forbid the trap on their own. They only matter as resting stops for pigeons from a far-away settlement, and that's why the ברייתא mentions one hundred מיל.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's thirty ריס is the normal distance for setting pigeon traps. Only where there are vineyards or dovecotes along the way, where pigeons can rest, does the ban on traps reach as far as one hundred מיל.

phrases.english: If you want, say: it's about dovecotes of a gentile,
and if you want, say: about ownerless ones,
and if you want, say: about his own.
phrases.notes: The dovecotes belong to the same person who is setting the trap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבה from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining ownership: the nearby dovecotes have no protected owner.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nearby dovecotes should forbid the trap on their own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dovecotes belong to a גוי, are הפקר, or are his own. So they only matter as resting points for pigeons from the far settlement.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק מרובה
steps.stepSummary: The פרק called מרובה comes to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק מרובה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new halacha is added here. It marks the end of the seventh פרק of בבא קמא, which is called מרובה.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of this פרק, taken from its first word

phrases.english: We will return to you, Merubba

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion ends.
